owner.name: QQ Chen
owner.headline: I ship AI products end to end — design, backend, iOS, App Store.
owner.blurb: Ten products built solo over the past year. Everything below is running right now: three are on the App Store, seven are live on the web. Each card opens with a walkthrough of what the product actually does.

products.name: TingZhai
products.subtitle: Podcast AI Notes
products.tagline: The worst thing about podcasts: you finish one and keep nothing.
products.role: Solo — backend, iOS, App Store submission
products.pitch: Hear something worth keeping while cooking or driving? Just say "note" out loud. No touching the phone, no wake word for Siri, playback never stops. AI turns it into something readable, then spaced repetition brings it back right before you forget.
highlights: Custom on-device wake word. Stress-tested against 127K characters of real Chinese transcripts — cut false triggers from 38 to 0.
Cross-tenant transcript cache: the same episode costs AI money once, not once per user. 86% hit rate, 7.07× reuse, US$0.82 per episode.
Spaced repetition (SM-2) — no competitor in this category ships it.
Found and fixed two App Store rejection risks pre-submission by running an adversarial review with a second AI agent.

products.name: Woordjes
products.subtitle: Dutch Vocabulary
products.tagline: Built because I was failing my own Dutch A2 exam.
products.role: Solo — backend, iOS, App Store submission
products.pitch: Original word list, free, no ads, no tracking. Started as a tool for my own exam prep and turned into a shipped app with a shared content layer across web and iOS.
highlights: Auto-illustrated concrete nouns via image generation — roughly 300 images for about US$2.
Frequency-based leveling so you learn common words first instead of memorising rare ones.
Same engine later produced the Japanese app — 95% of the code is shared, only the content layer differs.

products.name: Tango
products.subtitle: Japanese Vocabulary
products.tagline: JLPT levels assigned by word frequency, not by intuition.
products.role: Solo — backend, iOS, App Store submission
products.pitch: The second app off the same engine. The interesting part was the data: an earlier heuristic had quietly pushed advanced kanji compounds into N3, so I rebuilt leveling on a 44K-word frequency table.
highlights: Re-leveled the full deck against a frequency corpus — N1 leakage into lower levels dropped to zero.
Grammar cards and vocabulary cards share one spaced-repetition scheduler.
Proved the engine is reusable: shipping a second language took content work, not a rewrite.

products.name: MaiLuo
products.subtitle: Reasoning Canvas
products.tagline: Turn an article into the argument behind it.
products.pitch: Drop in a Markdown file or a YouTube link. It breaks the content into cards and draws edges between them — but only edges it can justify. The output isn't a summary; it's the author's reasoning path laid out where you can see it.
highlights: Every edge has to state why it exists. Unjustifiable connections are not drawn.
Two reading depths generated side by side, plus text-to-speech.
Four follow-up actions: enrich, health-check, borrow a card, diagram it.

products.name: Yike
products.subtitle: One Moment Journal
products.tagline: One moment a day grows into a forest.
products.pitch: Not a to-do list. It reserves one place for the single thing that mattered today. Each entry grows a tree, and the forest becomes evidence of where you've been.
highlights: The tree is proof of depth, not a gamification hook — a deliberate product decision after studying Forest.
Gumroad license keys auto-activate through a Supabase edge function.
Ships as an installable PWA and a native iOS build.

products.name: Miraa
products.subtitle: Speaking Practice
products.pitch: Listen for three seconds, repeat it back, get scored word by word. Twenty iterations produced the echo drill, dictation mode, spaced repetition and Japanese furigana annotation.
highlights: Per-word pronunciation scoring rather than one number for the whole sentence.
Hit and solved two iOS web-audio traps: reused audio elements breaking after first playback, and MediaRecorder producing empty blobs.

products.name: Yicheng
products.subtitle: Work Log
products.pitch: Sister product to Yike. Most work logs record what you did; this one also records what the work taught you. Entirely local storage — data never leaves the browser.
highlights: Zero backend by design: localStorage only, nothing to breach.
Three-axis structure instead of a flat task list.

products.name: YuQiao
products.subtitle: Language Exchange
products.tagline: The AI is a bridge that walks away.
products.role: Solo — full stack, built in one night
products.pitch: The hard part of language exchange isn't language, it's awkwardness. The AI sits in the middle feeding words and topics — then steps back once the two people are actually talking.
highlights: Success metric is inverted: the AI is working when it gets used less over time.
Real-time voice rooms.

products.name: Gongdu
products.subtitle: Reading Check-in
products.tagline: Alone you quit; together you don't.
products.pitch: A shared check-in wall for an early-rising reading group. You can see whether your group is up yet, which turns out to be the whole mechanism.
highlights: Real-time sync via Supabase.
Sunrise theme: the earlier you check in, the brighter the board.

products.name: Language Practice Hub
products.subtitle: Dutch A2 Exam Prep
products.tagline: My own exam prep, turned into something practisable.
products.pitch: Seventeen worked past-paper sets for the Dutch A2 speaking exam, plus a 14-day sprint plan and daily review.
highlights: Two question types kept structurally separate — mixing them was why earlier drafts didn't work.
Picture-response questions always ship with the actual image, never a description.
